milestone: Dev Graph milestone 1, ticket 'Dev-graph schema and snapshot builder on a synthetic fixture'
authority: CLAUDE.md §9.4. Not a constitutional amendment. The sets are data in runner/dev_graph/schema.py. Changing either is a schema change and needs a test.
decision: The dev graph uses a closed node-type set of seventeen types and a closed relationship set of ten predicates. Any other type or predicate is rejected at build time, naming the offending node or edge. related_to is not in the set: an untyped link has no defined traversal meaning.
direction: Every predicate reads source to target. The direction is declared on the spec and is not inferred from names.
effect_flag: A domain link says what a fact means (who does the work, what a package contributes to). An execution dependency says what must exist or hold first (a task consumes its predecessor, a deliverable is validated by its milestone). The impact planner will treat only execution dependencies as invalidation paths. The flag exists so assigned_to is never mistaken for a dependency.
derived_edges: The builder derives edges from record structure only: lead_partner, responsible_partner, contributing_partners, dependencies, objectives, task and deliverable membership, produced_by and milestone deliverables. Tier 3 declares no predicate of its own. Every derived edge passes validate_graph, which is public so a caller can check a candidate edge set without a build.

rejections.duplicate_id: the same declared key twice, within a file or across files. Names the id.
rejections.dangling_edge: an endpoint id that no node declares. Names the edge.
rejections.endpoint_type: an endpoint pair the predicate does not permit. Names the edge and the offending type.
rejections.unknown_predicate: a predicate outside the closed set, including related_to. Names the edge.
rejections.malformed_record: unreadable JSON, a record without its declared key, or a wrong shape. Names the file.
rejections.cardinality: a second target where the predicate allows one. Names the edge.

extension_rule: Adding a type or a predicate means editing the table in runner/dev_graph/schema.py and the test that pins the sets in tests/runner/test_dev_graph_snapshot.py. The document-snapshot ticket adds passage linkage and the impact planner ticket adds execution nodes. Each adds its own record.
cardinality: Declared per predicate and enforced by the validator for the single-target cardinalities: one_to_one and many_to_one allow at most one target per source and predicate. A second target is rejected with kind cardinality, naming the edge.
endpoint_scope: Endpoint pairs are the ones this milestone's tickets name. The builder produces the Tier 3 pairs today. The pairs on claim, passage, artifact_version, assessment, finding, change_request and revision_contract are reserved for the document-snapshot, package, planner and revision tickets, which add builder paths and tests without reopening this record.
